analysis.investment_thesis: DEEPAKNTR has an earnings yield of only ~5% (EBIT INR 1,095 Cr / EV ~INR 22,067 Cr) — well below Magic Formula minimums — while ROCE of 16.3% is also sub-threshold and the operating income has been contracting for three consecutive years. You are paying a premium price for a deteriorating earnings trajectory.
key_strengths: Impressive 9-year revenue CAGR of 22.1% demonstrating Deepak Nitrite's ability to scale from a niche intermediates player to a diversified chemical manufacturer
Near-debt-free balance sheet through FY24 (D/E 0.22) with strong equity build-up, giving financial flexibility for the current capex cycle
Consistent OCF positivity (5/5 years) with strong institutional ownership (DII at 23.46%) suggesting quality recognition
key_risks: Operating income has contracted from INR 1,607 Cr (FY22) to INR 1,095 Cr (FY25) — a 32% peak-to-trough decline; Magic Formula requires sustained EBIT, not cyclical peaks
Earnings yield of ~5% is roughly half the Magic Formula minimum of 12% — the market is pricing in a strong recovery that hasn't materialized yet
FCF turned sharply negative in FY25 (–INR 494 Cr) as capex jumped to INR 1,136 Cr and CWIP surged to INR 2,046 Cr — returns on this capital are speculative
red_flags: Net profit fell from INR 1,067 Cr (FY22) to INR 697 Cr (FY25) — a 35% decline — while the stock trades at P/E of 38.7x, implying the market is paying for FY22 earnings at FY25 prices
Borrowings jumped from INR 73 Cr (FY23) to INR 1,244 Cr (FY25) in a single year, reversing the debt reduction trend and adding leverage risk
Phenolics segment margins appear structurally pressured by global overcapacity; a multi-year recovery timeline is speculative
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Magic Formula math: EV = INR 20,979 + 1,267 – 179 = INR 22,067 Cr. EBIT = INR 1,095 Cr. Earnings Yield = 4.96% — the worst earnings yield in this group after DOMS and Delhivery. ROCE = 16.3%. Neither metric meets my thresholds. The stock is expensive for a business with declining earnings, and I don't invest based on 'what margins could be' — I invest based on what returns are actually being earned on capital today.

The phenolics cycle downturn has exposed how much of Deepak Nitrite's extraordinary FY20–FY22 profitability was cyclical, not structural. Until EBIT stabilizes and ROCE climbs convincingly above 20% while the stock re-rates to offer earnings yield above 12%, this remains a pass for the Magic Formula screen.
